decisions.decision: New Settings field 'Reprompt mode': Global | Per-credential. Global = every credential's reveal/copy requires master password, cached for a configurable grace window (default 30s), then re-locks. Per-credential = today's existing per-credential 'Require reprompt' flag, no grace window, asks every time.
decisions.rationale: User wants a universal reprompt option but the existing per-credential flag design should remain available for credentials that should never get a grace window. A single settings toggle lets the user choose the model without losing either.

decisions.decision: Login/reprompt master-password delay: do NOT reduce Argon2id KDF cost (m=64MiB t=3 p=4, core/src/crypto.rs:48) as part of this phase's gap closure. Add a loading animation instead (G-08-7).
decisions.rationale: Audited: measured 1961ms per derive_key call in a DEBUG build (npm run tauri dev always uses debug). Login calls it twice (~4s), reprompt once (~2s) - matches user's complaint. The KDF params are intentional and already reviewed as correct in SECURITY_CONCERNS.md (flagged there only for missing web-mode rate-limiting, not for being mistuned). Could not empirically confirm release-build timing - release build fails in this environment for an unrelated pre-existing reason (rusqlite's bundled-sqlcipher-vendored-openssl feature needs a Perl module, Locale::Maketext::Simple, not installed here). Unoptimized-vs-optimized Rust for tight crypto loops is a well-documented 5-20x gap, so real (release) delay is expected to be a few hundred ms. User explicitly deferred the KDF-cost decision to later, after a real release-build measurement.

decisions.decision: A site with saved credentials should be deletable (cascading to its credentials) behind a confirmation popup, not blocked outright as it is today.
decisions.rationale: User wants one clear cascade-delete action with a safety confirmation, not a forced one-by-one credential deletion first.
